articles.body:
Mortgage rates decline for first time in 2 months

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate dipped this week to 7.32 percent , according to new data from Freddie Mac.

© George Walker IV, The Associated Press

That marked a decline from last week’s average rate of 7.4 percent , and the first weekly decline since the week ending on Aug. 20.

The average 30-year mortgage rate has spiked from 5.98 percent the week before the Iran war, as rising bond yields and oil prices have pushed up borrowing costs for prospective homebuyers.

Thirty-year mortgage rates held steady at 7.4 percent last week, a pause after seven consecutive weekly increases. Despite this week’s decline, the average 30-year rate is still higher than it was at the end of all but one week dating to Thanksgiving 2023 .

The average 15-year mortgage rate also declined from 6.71 percent last week to 6.68 percent this week .

High mortgage rates have bottlenecked the housing market, with pending home sales in September falling by 7.3 percent month-over-month and 11.3 percent on an annual basis, according to data from the National Association of Realtors (NAR).

Dr. Lawrence Yun, the chief economist at the NAR, faulted “fast-rising” mortgage rates for the weak housing market in September.

“Although job growth and income gains can support home purchases, housing affordability is more affected by changes in mortgage rates,” Yun said in a statement.

Yun noted that mortgage rates “have already risen much more” than the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate hikes .

Fed officials raised rates by a quarter point last month and will meet again next week to decide whether to hike again amid persistent inflation.

“However, increasing energy prices and the resulting inflationary pressure are highly uncertain ,” Yun acknowledged.

President Trump on Thursday sought to lower housing and mortgage costs via an executive order, which directs Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) Director Bill Pulte to create a pilot program to cancel borrowers’ mortgage insurance premiums once they have satisfied equity requirements.

Trump is also directing Pulte to expand the FHFA’s title insurance waiver pilot into a permanent program , which will provide borrowers with “cost-friendly alternatives” to title insurance, the order states.

articles.title: Michigan, Ohio Gas Prices Spike Further Amid Refinery Breakdown
articles.summary: Gas prices in two Midwestern battleground states saw further hikes on Thursday as the region’s market grapples with a refinery issue in Illinois.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Gas prices in two Midwestern battleground states saw further hikes on Thursday as the region's market grapples with a refinery issue in Illinois.

In Michigan, prices rose to $4.74 a gallon on Thursday, up from $4.59 a gallon on Wednesday, according to GasBuddy, a fuel savings app that tracks prices in live time. In Ohio, prices stood at $4.34 a gallon, up from $4.05 a gallon on Wednesday. GasBuddy's prices differ slightly from those released by AAA, which issues nightly updates on prices.

A shut-down of a key unit at ExxonMobil Holdings Corp.'s Joliet, Illinois, refinery had already pushed prices significantly higher on Wednesday in both states.

Polls show tight Senate races in both states, with the cost of living and pump prices top voter issues in the midterm elections 12 days from now. Democrats must hold on to their seat in Michigan, a state won by President Donald Trump in 2024, if they hope to flip control of the US Senate. Republicans similarly see Ohio as crucial to maintaining their majority.

The impacts are spreading throughout the broader area, with price hikes in Wisconsin and Indiana, as well as Illinois.

articles.body: MUMBAI: Rising crude oil prices with the Indian crude basket at a 14-year high, fresh weakness of the rupee after an eight-session gain and sliding Asian markets weighed on investor sentiment on Dalal Street on Thursday.As a result, sensex showed a weak trend from the start of the session and closed 460 points or 0.6% lower at 73,249 points. On NSE, Nifty lost 124 points or 0.5% to close at 22,688 points.On Thursday, the average price for the Indian crude basket for Oct hit a high of $120 per barrel, up from the recent high of $114.5 in April. This is the highest level since it hit $123.6 in March 2012, data from Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell of ministry of petroleum & natural gas showed. The Indian crude basket is a derived basket of two types of crude oil, Brent and Oman & Dubai, that are imported by Indian refiners.This jump in the Indian basket came as Brent crude prices shot up to over the $112 per-barrel mark, the highest level seen since May this year. This came on the back of talks of escalation of the war between US and Iran in the Persian Gulf region.Shooting oil prices also weakened the rupee that, after an eight-session rally, reversed trend to hover close to the 95/$ level, having fallen 36 paise. Weakness across major Asian markets also made Indian investors nervous, market players said.According to Ankur Punj, MD, Equirus Wealth, India market’s downward spiral continued due to external factors as a fresh escalation in the West Asia conflict pushed oil prices up. “Weak Asian and European market cues and a steep fall in the rupee against the dollar further (affected investor) sentiment,” Punj wrote in a note. “While (corporate) earnings have been a mixed bag so far, concerns over an uptick in inflation due to higher crude oil prices and persistent (foreign fund) selling in local shares could further drive investors to safe haven dollar assets.”Among the major Asian market indices, Kospi in Korea closed 3.5% down, Hang Seng in Hong Kong closed 3% down, Nikkei in Japan was down 2.7% at the close while Shanghai Composite in China closed 1.5% lower. At the close of Thursday’s session, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net sellers at Rs 3,459 crore while domestic funds were net buyers at Rs 2,891 crore, provisional data on BSE showed. articles.title: Videos, the new gateway reshaping online retail
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Indians are no longer just shopping; they are video-shopping.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Indians are no longer just shopping; they are video-shopping. Videos drive a lot of traction on online platforms such as Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and Meesho. Consumers scroll through creator-led content reels or shorts, discovering a host of new brands and products with many eventually clicking on the ‘buy’ tab, often embedded in them. The trend is more popular among Gen Z shoppers and consumers residing in smaller towns, companies said.For one, there’s live commerce wherein creators showcase a product or give demonstrations in real time. The other format is shortform shoppable videos which may or may not always feature creators and may not be live, but they allow people to buy products without leaving the video stream by way of links included within them. Live commerce and shoppable videos have both scaled to collectively create a content-to-commerce ecosystem. For Bengaluru-based IT professional Sanjeet Singh, influencer reels play a big role in product discovery. “Reels give me an idea of what the product is,” Singh said.Social media platforms such as Instagram and YouTube had already made access easier than ever—people sat at their homes, browsed through videos, subscribing to influencer-led recommendations and buying products. Platforms took note of the shopping habit and launched their own video and live formats.Amazon, for instance, launched Live in 2022 while players such as Myntra and Meesho joined in after a couple of years or so. The strategy seemed to have worked—creator-led discovery has influenced the shopping journeys of nearly two crore consumers on Amazon so far in 2026 while for Meesho, active order-generating content grew by over 140% to 1.7 million in Q1FY27, the firms said.Besides, all the e-commerce companies have active accounts on platforms such as Instagram wherein they collaborate with influencers to market their products and sale events, amplifying visibility.Creator-led commerce will become a key driver for e-commerce growth, contributing nearly $25 billion in gross merchandise value (GMV) by 2030, a joint April study by Deloitte and Google showed. “Creator content will scale significantly, with creator-owned storefronts and online videos becoming instantly shoppable. Eventually, these formats will also help onboard 50-60 million new online shoppers from tier 2 markets by effectively addressing key barriers around trust, product understanding, and quality,” analysts said in the report.Cos’ video strategyAmazon has scaled Live beyond real-time product demonstrations and creator recommendations to shortform, shoppable video experiences that are integrated directly into the shopping journey. “Short-form shopping videos complement live commerce and help keep product discovery contextual and engaging. The video format helps customers understand how a product works, see it in a real-life context, compare options, ask questions and move directly towards purchase,” said Nidhi Thakkar, head of social commerce, emerging countries at Amazon.Nearly 70% of creator-led purchases on Amazon marketplace have come from non-metro cities, including cities such as Bathinda, Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore and Dehradun. “This reflects the role regional creators are playing in helping customers discover products through content that is relevant to their language, context and communities,” Thakkar added.Myntra launched Ultimate Glam Clan (UGC) in Aug 2024—a shopper creator programme which enables customers to create fashion and beauty content around products they discover and shop on the platform. UGC grew to more than eight million sign-ups and 12 million cumulative pieces of content as of Sept 2026, the company claimed.It also built Glamstream in July 2025, which brings together creator-led video, entertainment and commerce within the Myntra app. “Video is increasingly becoming an important part of the discovery journey, helping consumers explore fashion and beauty through creator recommendations, styling inspiration and realworld context. Users engaging with social commerce content convert around 10% better than those who do not, highlighting the role of content in influencing purchase decisions,” said Deepash Jain, vice-president, marketing, Myntra, adding that the format has enabled platforms to move beyond traditional catalogue-led shopping.Flipkart’s video commerce ecosystem spans shortform videos, live shopping, creator-led product demos, Q&As, gamified formats and seamless in-video shopping journeys. “Shopping in India is increasingly being shaped by what consumers watch, share and trust,” said Ramesh Gururaja, senior vice president, consumer products and growth, FCC, Ads and Cleartrip at Flipkart.You use AI every day. articles.summary: MUMBAI: The maiden public offering for Jio Platforms, through which the company is raising Rs 30,213 crore, making it the largest such offer in India, was
articles.body: MUMBAI: The maiden public offering for Jio Platforms, through which the company is raising Rs 30,213 crore, making it the largest such offer in India, was subscribed over five times at the close of bidding on Day 2. Institutional investors continued to lead the bidding process—that had helped the IPO to get fully subscribed within the first 100 minutes of opening on Day 1—with high-net-worth investors (HNIs) following closely, data from the bourses showed.The retail portion of the offer—that was subscribed 70% on Day 1—was also fully subscribed on Thursday, with the Day 2 closing data showing 1.5 times subscription for 8.5 crore shares that are on offer.At the close of Day 2, the total demand for Jio shares was worth about Rs 3.7 lakh crore, including the anchor portion. On Thursday, the institutional (QIB) part of the IPO, in which a little over 4.9 crore shares were offered, was subscribed nearly 13.3 times, while the HNI portion, in which about 3.6 crore shares were reserved, was subscribed six times. Usually, in most IPOs, institutional players apply on the last day of the offer.Exchange data also showed that the portion reserved for employees was subscribed over two times while the part reserved for RIL shareholders was subscribed a little over four times.In the unofficial market, speculators are betting that the company will be listing at about Rs 1,360, a mark-up (also called the grey market premium or GMP) of Rs 241 over the upper limit of the IPO price band. The current GMP is slightly lower than Rs 273, the highest level seen a day before the IPO opened, but much higher than the opening quote of Rs 148 on Oct 4, quotes from websites tracking the trend in the unofficial market for shares showed. articles.title: Yes Bank Additional Tier 1 bondholders seek interest payment
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Retail bondholders of YES Bank have asked Axis Trustee Services, the debenture trustee, to secure payment of overdue coupons (interest payments)
articles.body: MUMBAI: Retail bondholders of YES Bank have asked Axis Trustee Services, the debenture trustee, to secure payment of overdue coupons (interest payments) on the bank’s Additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds, restore their holdings in demat accounts and seek regulatory intervention, days after Supreme Court dismissed appeals against Bombay high court’s ruling that quashed the March 2020 write-off.The YES Bank AT1 Retail Bond Holders Association cited Companies Act and Sebi obligations in seeking an explanation for non-payment of the 9% bond coupon due Oct 18, three days after the Oct 15 court order restoring the bonds. It also demanded payment of coupons skipped in 2020-25 and arrangements for the forthcoming Dec 23 coupon on 9.5% bonds.According to analysts, revisiting past coupons raises legal and accounting issues. The write-off was recognised in profit and loss, so restoring the bonds could affect past profits. Coupon payments on high-risk AT1 bonds are also contingent on the bank’s financial performance.The association asked Axis Trustee to disclose YES Bank’s position on each missed coupon, cancellation notices and correspondence since March 2020, including any reliance on contractual discretion or record dates. articles.title: At €310 billion, Union minister Piyush Goyal eyes 10x rise in Indo-German trade
articles.summary: BERLIN: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Thursday set an ambitious target of increasing bilateral trade with Germany tenfold to 310 billion
articles.body: BERLIN: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Thursday set an ambitious target of increasing bilateral trade with Germany tenfold to 310 billion euros, urging businesses to forge partnerships ahead of implementation of the India-EU free trade agreement (FTA).At the inauguration of the India Centre and Indo-German Business Forum in Berlin, Goyal said the FTA could be signed by Dec and implemented within four to five months. “We had 31.5 billion euros (in 2025) and (if) we were to be able to add a zero to that, make it 310 billion euros. How would that sound? Now, we can certainly make that happen,” he said, emphasising the need to draw up concrete plans to realise the ambition.Goyal is on a visit to Germany and the Netherlands from Oct 22 to 27, leading a delegation of around 100 Indian businesses and startups to explore opportunities in trade, investment and industrial cooperation. The minister said Germany’s precision engineering and commitment to quality complemented India’s infrastructure expansion, digital capabilities and young, skilled workforce, creating scope for collaboration in manufacturing, technology and supply chains. He said the two countries had little to compete with each other and could together strengthen supply chain resilience and have a transformational impact on each other’s economies.He asked businesses to start identifying customers and investors, exploring partnerships and aligning product quality and pricing with market requirements rather than wait for the FTA to come into effect. “This is the time partnerships need to be forged. This is the time connects need to be made with potential customers, collaborators, investors,” Goyal said, adding that companies must prepare to “trade, invest smarter, faster and get the best out of this agreement”.Negotiations for the India-EU FTA concluded in Jan this year following talks between PM Narendra Modi and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Goyal said the agreement had received unanimous support from all 27 EU member states and expressed confidence that the remaining process would move rapidly. India-EU trade stood at 118 billion euros in 2025.Goyal outlined priorities for India and Germany, including strengthening economic security, creating industrial opportunities through the green transition and advancing emerging technologies. He called for closer cooperation in apprenticeships and skilling, areas in which Germany has considerable expertise.Germany’s minister for economic affairs and energy, Katherina Reiche, said bilateral trade remained below potential, with India not featuring among Germany’s top 20 trading partners despite goods trade worth around 31 billion euros in 2025.“We could at least double the trade amount we have right now,” she said, calling for greater investment and industrial partnerships. articles.summary: BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of
articles.body: BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. articles.title: 'Orelha-de-elefante': moradora encontra planta misteriosa no quintal, e especialista alerta que espécie é tóxica | G1
articles.standfirst: Uma moradora de São Bernardo do Campo enviou carta e fotos para identificar a planta; agrônomo confirmou suspeita sobre a família Araceae e fez alerta sobre riscos à saúde.
articles.summary: Uma moradora de São Bernardo do Campo enviou carta e fotos para identificar a planta; agrônomo confirmou suspeita sobre a família Araceae e fez alerta sobre riscos à saúde.
articles.body:
Uma planta misteriosa que brotou no quintal chamou a atenção de Maria Hernandes, moradora de São Bernardo do Campo, na Grande São Paulo.

Para descobrir qual era a espécie, ela enviou uma carta escrita à mão e duas fotos ao Globo Rural . Maria desconfiava que a planta pertencia à família Araceae, a mesma da taioba.

O agrônomo Chukichi Kurozawa, consultor do programa, confirmou a suspeita e identificou a planta como orelha-de-elefante-panduriforme.

Ela chama a atenção pelas folhas grandes, enrugadas e onduladas. Segundo o especialista, a espécie é cultivada principalmente como planta ornamental.

Apesar da aparência, ela oferece riscos à saúde. Tanto as folhas quanto os rizomas, caules subterrâneos responsáveis pelo armazenamento de nutrientes, são tóxicos e não devem ser consumidos.

articles.title: Treasury proposes curbs on high-tech investments in China, Russia, North Korea
articles.summary: The Treasury Department on Thursday proposed a rule to curb American high-tech investments, including AI, outbound to U.S. adversaries like China, Russia, North Korea and other “countries of concern.” The rule expands restrictions in the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) on hypersonic systems and quantum information technologies, high-performance computing and supercomputing, as well as AI.…
articles.body:
The Treasury Department on Thursday proposed a rule to curb American high-tech investments, including AI, outbound to U.S. adversaries like China, Russia, North Korea and other “countries of concern.”

The rule expands restrictions in the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) on hypersonic systems and quantum information technologies, high-performance computing and supercomputing, as well as AI. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added biotechnology to the regulations.

The department’s proposal would apply to investments exceeding $50,000 and excludes financial investments such as stock purchases.

Treasury officials said these rules implement what Congress passed with the 2025 Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security (COIN) Act.

“The proposed regulations would strengthen the existing Outbound Investment Security Program to prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies that threaten U.S. national security,” Bessent said in a statement.

“This important step also helps promote our commitment to an open investment environment by providing clarity to U.S. and foreign investors as well as an opportunity for them to provide feedback on the proposed regulations,” Bessent added.

Former President Biden launched the program in 2023 via an executive order placing restrictions on outbound investments in sectors like semiconductors and quantum computing sent to China. The Treasury Department later established the program as OISP.

The proposal is a first step “in a fairly long process to get to changes which presumably will be more enforcement-minded, to put more teeth behind the outbound investment program,” former U.S. trade official Ryan Majerus told The Associated Press .

Public comments about the proposal will be made before the Treasury issues a final rule.

The U.S. and China have agreed to ease tensions over their competing technological advancements, though both countries have restricted the export of sensitive technology and critical products.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) on Monday ordered that products from the Chinese AI startup DeepSeek be removed from federal agency IT systems, citing “multiple threat vectors.”

DHS warned that some of DeepSeek’s commonly used applications could transfer “sensitive data to the PRC [People’s Republic of China] if used by U.S. government or vendors.”

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Tuesday that Beijing “consistently opposes overstretching the concept of national security and politicizing tech and trade issues.”

The Chinese Ministry of Commerce accused the U.S. of trying to suppress China under “the guise of national security,” and said the order disregarded agreements reached between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, The Associated Press reported.

“China will closely monitor the situation and take all necessary measures to firmly defend its legitimate rights and interests,” the commerce ministry stated, per the AP.

articles.title: US tech stocks tumble as investors fret over AI spending
articles.summary: Tech-heavy Nasdaq falls 2.6 percent as debate rages over whether AI is a bubble.
articles.body:
US tech stocks have dropped sharply amid market jitters over the sustainability of companies’ enormous capital investments in AI.

The Nasdaq Composite, which is dominated by tech firms linked to the AI boom, fell 2.6 percent on Thursday, its steepest fall since the index tumbled 4.2 percent on June 5.

The broader S&P 500 slid 1.21 percent, the benchmark’s biggest drop since a 1.52 percent decline on July 29.

Apart from Apple, each of the “Magnificent 7”, which make up more than one-third of the overall market, saw substantial losses.

Meta dropped nearly 7 percent after it raised its projected capital spending for this year to $135bn to $145bn in its latest earnings report, even as the Facebook parent company’s net profit fell short of expectations.

Amazon fell 4.6 percent, while Nvidia dropped 4.4 percent.

Tesla and Alphabet both fell 3.1 percent, while Microsoft declined 2.2 percent.

The sell-off extended to other major tech players, including Intel and Advanced Micro Devices, both of which fell about 8 percent, and Broadcom, which slid 4.3 percent.

After the losses, the Nasdaq is about 5.8 percent off its all-time high, reached on October 6.

Rising oil prices since February, due to the fallout of the US-Israel war on Iran, added to the downbeat mood.

Brent crude futures rose 4 percent on Thursday and continued to climb on Friday morning, taking the international benchmark above $114.20 a barrel, its highest since May.

Major stock markets in Asia opened lower on Friday, following the losses on Wall Street.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 fell more than 2 percent in morning trading before recovering some ground, while South Korea’s KOSPI dropped as much as 3.5 percent.

The Hang Seng Index in Hong Kong fell about 0.5 percent.

Jay Goldberg, a senior analyst at Seaport Research Partners in San Francisco, said the swings in the market appeared to be driven more by sentiment than underlying fundamentals.

“In short, nothing has changed. Investors have just decided to be afraid this week. Everyone I speak to points to a different cause for the downfall … It’s just a giant wall of worry,” Goldberg told Al Jazeera.

“There are legitimate concerns about the AI trade, but this level of shift in the markets is driven much more by investor sentiment than any tangible reason.”

US tech companies’ huge investments in AI have stoked intense debate about whether a market bubble is forming similar to the one that preceded the 2000 dot-com crash.

While some Wall Street analysts view current levels of investment in datacentres and graphics processing units as unsustainable, others argue that AI will revolutionise society to a degree that justifies the eye-watering sums involved.

Global AI investment is forecast to reach $2.7 trillion in 2026 and $3.6 trillion in 2027, according to technology insights company Gartner.

articles.title: Starting a food business? FSSAI offers help to navigate safety rules and approvals
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For entrepreneurs launching food businesses, navigating food safety regulations can be as challenging as developing a product.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For entrepreneurs launching food businesses, navigating food safety regulations can be as challenging as developing a product. From securing licences to getting labelling and product claims right, gaps in regulatory understanding can lead to avoidable errors and delays.To address these challenges, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) will operationalise a dedicated Start-Up Cell next month officials said. The cell will help emerging food businesses understand regulatory requirements and seek guidance on compliance.According to an FSSAI social media post, start-ups can approach the cell every Wednesday during a dedicated online session to get their queries addressed. They can also email questions to startupcell@fssai.gov.in.The cell will provide guidance on food business licensing and registration, product standards and categorisation, approvals, labelling and advertising claims, testing, imports, e-commerce compliance, novel foods and nutraceuticals.These are areas where regulatory clarity can be particularly important for new businesses seeking to bring products to market while meeting food safety requirements.However, the cell will offer advisory guidance, not exemptions from existing rules or automatic approvals. Licensing, approval and enforcement decisions will remain with the competent authorities. Queries requiring legal interpretation will be vetted by FSSAI’s Legal Division.The authority said information shared for query resolution would be handled confidentially and anonymised for policy analysis. The cell will also provide a channel for start-ups to flag recurring regulatory challenges and seek information about FSSAI initiatives and guidance materials.For entrepreneurs, the initiative could offer a single point of contact for understanding applicable food safety requirements before products reach consumers. articles.title: Luis, jubilado, dejó España y se mudó a Tailandia con 68 años: "Con 20.000 euros puedes construirte una casa y vivir tranquilo"
articles.standfirst: Vive en el noreste de Tailandia con su pensión y explica las diferencias que encuentra con su vida anterior en España
articles.summary: Vive en el noreste de Tailandia con su pensión y explica las diferencias que encuentra con su vida anterior en España
articles.body: Luis tiene 68 años, está jubilado y ha encontrado en Tailandia una forma de vida que, según explica, encaja mejor con sus necesidades actuales. Reside en la región de Isan, en el noreste del país asiático, lejos de los destinos turísticos más conocidos. Allí ha construido una vivienda sencilla con el dinero que ganó durante su vida laboral en España y disfruta de una rutina que describe como más tranquila. Su historia fue recogida por La Vanguardia y en la entrevista, el jubilado explicó que en España su pensión le permitía vivir con ciertas limitaciones económicas, mientras que en Tailandia considera que dispone de un mayor margen para afrontar los gastos cotidianos. Uno de los datos que más llaman la atención de su testimonio es el coste que atribuye a la construcción de una vivienda en la zona donde reside. "Una persona con 20.000 euros aquí puede hacerse una casa", afirmó. La casa que construyó es sencilla y está levantada sobre un terreno que pertenece a su mujer, de nacionalidad tailandesa. En la entrevista también explicó que los extranjeros se enfrentan a restricciones para poseer terrenos en Tailandia, por lo que es importante conocer la legislación local antes de plantearse una mudanza de este tipo. El día de Luis comienza antes del amanecer. A veces se levanta a las tres y media o a las cuatro de la mañana, prepara café y se sienta en el porche de su casa. Después sale a caminar con sus perros y organiza la jornada sin las prisas que, según cuenta, asociaba a su vida anterior. El jubilado también destaca el coste de algunos gastos domésticos. Según su relato, la factura de la electricidad ronda los 60 euros mensuales, una cantidad que puede variar en función de la vivienda, el consumo y las tarifas aplicables. Su decisión tampoco responde únicamente a motivos económicos. Luis valora especialmente el ambiente que encuentra en su localidad y la posibilidad de llevar un ritmo de vida menos acelerado. "Te das cuenta de que muchas cosas no eran tan importantes como piensas", señaló al hablar de su adaptación. La experiencia de Luis no significa que Tailandia sea necesariamente una opción más económica o adecuada para todos los jubilados españoles. Antes de trasladarse a otro país es necesario estudiar cuestiones como la residencia legal, la fiscalidad, el acceso a la sanidad, los seguros médicos y las condiciones para adquirir o utilizar una vivienda. En el caso de Luis, la situación de su pareja y el hecho de contar con una vivienda construida en la zona forman parte de sus circunstancias particulares. También explicó que ha tenido dificultades para conseguir un seguro médico privado debido a su historial de salud.

articles.title: EU entering winter with lowest gas reserves on record, IEA boss warns
articles.summary: Al Jazeera interviews Fatih Birol in Berlin as the Iran war disrupts global energy supplies.
articles.body:
Berlin, Germany – Europe is entering winter with historically low gas reserves and cannot withstand further supply shocks, Fatih Birol, head of the International Energy Agency, has warned, as the US-Israel war on Iran disrupts global supply chains.

Speaking to Al Jazeera on the sidelines of an international conference in Berlin on Wednesday, Birol said all regions are being hit by energy disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz but that Europe is particularly vulnerable and will likely face rising costs of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in the coming months – even if peace returns to the Gulf today.

“The best day for a ceasefire would have been yesterday,” the energy economist, whose agency advises wealthy member nations and coordinates emergency responses, said.

“Normally before the winter, European countries have a lot of gas stocks, but the gas stocks we have while we are entering this winter are much lower than historical averages,” he said, adding that Europe’s gas is competing with that of Asian countries, which are even more dependent on the Middle East.

“I think if we have a harsh winter, we may see higher prices of natural gas in Europe,” Birol said, adding that the increasingly political nature of energy adds to the uncertainty. “Life will not be easy for Europe this year and also next year.”

European nations have long relied on imported gas to generate electricity for industries and warm homes in the freezing winter. Nearly a 10th of the continent’s LNG transited through the Hormuz Strait before the war. However, Iran’s attacks on vessels have plummeted imports.

As the winter chill settles, the European Union’s natural gas storage is only 72 percent full, down from the usual 90 percent. The shortfall is equivalent to the energy needed to power 10 to 12 million homes, analysts say.

EU energy ministers are now mulling over whether they should ask households and businesses to ration consumption, according to news reports.

Birol said he had long thought about the dangers of relying on the Strait of Hormuz. In fact, he said, his standard question to recruits seeking to join his agency was often: What would they do if the strait shuts down today?

The fallout has hardly come as a surprise. The flare-ups in the alternative Bab al-Mandeb strait, he added, have only worsened things.

“World leaders, how do they think?” Birol, who was born in Turkiye, said in his usual measured tone.

“I am really disappointed that governments didn’t take the necessary measures. Now, everybody is in a hurry, taking measures; the Middle East countries are building new pipelines, expanding the new pipelines that are bypassing the Strait of Hormuz … but in my view, these efforts should have been done much earlier.”

Europe’s historical over-reliance to blame

The EU, whose ageing refineries have processed less crude in recent years, also faces shortages of imported refined products such as the diesel that powers the bloc’s trucking, agricultural and industrial sectors.

Birol said Ukraine’s attacks on Russian refineries were also behind a looming diesel scarcity. About a third of Russian deliveries have stopped coming, he said.

When the Group of Seven (G7) nations agreed to push 400 million barrels of crude and diesel from their strategic reserves in March, it was Birol who coordinated how those emergency stocks reached global markets – the third time he has had to oversee emergency stock releases since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

For years, the energy economist said, his agency warned that the bloc was too tethered to Russia’s fuel, and that it had turned away too early from nuclear-generated power, which gave countries domestic leverage.

When Russia invaded Ukraine, his warnings manifested after Moscow cut gas supplies in retaliation for sanctions. The EU plans to permanently phase out Russian gas, but amid the Gulf crisis, members like France have again stepped up orders.

Industry experts say emergency reserves that hit the market have limited use, as some estimate only a few months will be covered.

But Birol argued that his agency recorded real impact – a $20 drop in soaring oil prices immediately after the G7 countries agreed to release 100 billion barrels of crude oil and diesel earlier this month.

Prices are, however, on the rise again. Gas has surged by 140 percent since February, and Brent crude is trading well above $100.

Whatever happens now, the war will be felt for months, Birol pointed out, adding that it has irrevocably altered how energy will travel around the world.

It is also altering Europe’s politics, Birol noted. Russia has wielded gas as a weapon. And populist parties, from France to Germany, are capturing growing public anger to frame mainstream governments as incompetent.

“I have never ever seen the dark and long shadow of geopolitics so dominant in the energy sector,” Birol mused. “The world has gone through so many difficult periods, but this is the worst in terms of the geopolitics dominating the energy game. Energy is not currently considered a business but a political leverage. As an energy man, this worries me.”

The EU still has about 80 percent of its emergency stocks, and Birol hopes he will not have to oversee a fourth release. But the world’s supply can’t take more shocks, he said.

“I really hope that both of the straits will be unconditionally opened sometime soon; otherwise, in the energy world, we don’t have much more buffer zones to still keep the prices at a certain level (as) we have today,” he concluded.
